key_insight: SpikeDS improves 3D MRI prediction of perineural invasion by combining binary spike communication with window-level spatial pruning to keep attention efficient.
clinical_relevance: This could help identify cholangiocarcinoma patients at higher risk of perineural invasion using a more computationally practical 3D MRI model.
method: Uses a dual-sparsity spiking transformer for volumetric MRI analysis
Applies Window-based Expert Mixture Spiking Attention to focus only on high-firing-rate windows
Uses Cross-Window Spiking Self-Attention so pruned windows can still provide global context
evidence_signal: In 139 cholangiocarcinoma patients evaluated with 5-fold cross-validation, SpikeDS achieved AUC 0.753 while using only 14.4 mJ.
watch_item: The study is based on a relatively small single-cohort dataset, so external validation is needed before broader deployment.
paper_title: SpikeDS: Dual Sparsity Spikformer for Perineural Invasion Prediction in 3D MRI
